video_title: Raoul Pal: How To Get Rich In Crypto Before AI Takes Over
gist: Raoul Pal argues crypto is in an elongated mid-cycle correction (like 2020), not a cycle top, because flat US liquidity was absorbed by the AI trade; he expects bank lending and a steepening yield curve to restart liquidity, with Bitcoin ~1.5-2 standard deviations cheap versus Nasdaq, its log trend and liquidity. He frames AI as a 'deflationary nuclear bomb' heading to an economic singularity around 2030-2035, values layer-1s by a 'lights-off' test, flags agent/human identity as an overlooked blockchain use case, and recommends a simple, unleveraged core of BTC, ETH, SOL plus SUI/Zcash (or 50/50 Nasdaq-Bitcoin).

themes.theme: Liquidity regime: banks, yield curve, Greenspan '97 playbook

insights.claim: US liquidity growth has been flat after government shutdowns, the Iran war, higher oil, rates and dollar, and the limited liquidity available went to the AI trade; when AI went sideways, money rotated into crypto, showing there is not enough liquidity for both.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Crypto upside is gated on a broad liquidity restart, and AI and crypto currently compete for the same marginal dollar.

insights.claim: The debasement mechanism is shifting from central bank balance sheet expansion to bank lending, with officials like Scott Bessent and Kevin Warsh signaling the banking system must do the work, needed because hyperscalers are borrowing the most money ever.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Watch bank credit growth and yield-curve steepness rather than Fed balance sheet as the key liquidity indicator.

insights.claim: Banks have been held back from lending because the yield curve was too flat and bonds too volatile; once that clears and the curve steepens, liquidity flows properly and can fund everything at once.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Yield-curve steepening is the trigger to watch for a broad risk-asset rally including crypto.

insights.claim: Policy is replaying Greenspan's 1997 playbook: a dovish Fed chair acting hawkish, one token hike, while letting productivity-driven non-inflationary growth play out; the government funds at the short end while hyperscalers with ~50% margins fund at the long end regardless of rates.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Higher long-end yields need not derail the AI capex boom or risk assets in this framework.

insights.claim: Higher bond yields can act as net stimulus in aging, saver-heavy economies (US, Japan) because retirees and pension plans receive more interest income; in Japan the feared bond blowup merely steepened the curve and banks started lending massively.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Rising rates are not automatically bearish; the distributional winners are bondholders while the indebted middle class loses.

insights.claim: Nominal GDP growth is around 8%, and Pal expects inflation to be swapped for productivity growth, so GDP rises while inflation stabilizes, justifying higher bond yields to compete with high equity returns; the danger is only the short end rising too fast.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Long-end yield increases may signal growth, not stress; watch the front end for real danger.

insights.claim: Pal does not believe rates return to zero soon, arguing the largest technological shift in history cannot occur in the shortest period without permanently changing the rate regime.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Don't plan housing or portfolio decisions around a return to 2020-21 era rates.

insights.claim: The current crypto drawdown is not a cycle top but an elongated mid-cycle correction similar to 2020, because there was no liquidity down-cycle, only a flat period.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Pal rejects the four-year-cycle bear thesis; positioning for continuation rather than a deep bear.

insights.claim: Bitcoin reached about two standard deviations oversold versus Nasdaq on a log-regression channel, about 1.5 standard deviations below its own log trend since 2017, and similarly cheap versus liquidity.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Statistically stretched-cheap readings support accumulation and mean-reversion trades.

insights.claim: With global liquidity at all-time highs and US liquidity close to all-time highs, even a rotation-driven catch-up could take crypto almost back to its all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Crypto has a gap to close versus liquidity even without new liquidity growth.
insights.quote: Global liquidity is at alltime highs.

insights.claim: Something broke in crypto on 10/10 (an unexplained event) that drained liquidity and users; wallet counts have not recovered since.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: On-chain user/wallet recovery is a confirmation signal still missing.
insights.quote: in 1010 and nobody still knows what happened

insights.claim: The prior rally never reached even one standard deviation overbought versus trend; Pal would take profits/lifestyle chips only at 1-2 standard deviations above trend.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete, rules-based profit-taking band instead of calendar-cycle selling.

insights.claim: Trading the four-year cycle looks good on paper but fails in practice: sellers rarely buy back at the lows with the same size because they fear another leg down, and many are now trapped because the market bottomed earlier than the cycle predicted.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Cycle-timing sellers risk being left out if a super-cycle develops.
insights.quote: can't buy back in at the lows with the same size

insights.claim: The 2024-onward run is one cycle driven sequentially by Bitcoin ETFs, then digital asset treasuries (DATs) and meme coins, followed by a clear-out event, possibly leading to an 'everything works' phase.
insights.speaker: Michael (host) / Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Next leg would need broader on-chain adoption rather than another wrapper product.

insights.claim: Gold now trades as a pure financial-conditions asset tracking the dollar, short rates and especially the yield curve; after its biggest move since 1980 it needs to calm down, and a steepening curve should help gold recover while liquidity rotates into the Bitcoin debasement story.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Gold-to-Bitcoin rotation is a potential catalyst; the yield curve is the shared driver.

insights.claim: Pal rejects the diminishing-returns thesis for crypto: Bitcoin targets a share of finite global savings, but smart contracts have infinite use cases plus an infinite population of agents, so 'there is no top'.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Smart-contract platforms may have more asymmetric upside than Bitcoin under this view.

themes.theme: AI as a deflationary nuclear bomb & economic singularity

insights.claim: AI is replacing humans with a new apex intelligence and will make 2030-2035 the most deflationary event in history, to the point where the value of money becomes unclear.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Long-run deflationary pressure supports scarce/network assets and challenges nominal savings.
insights.quote: I call it like a deflationary nuclear bomb

insights.claim: Early deflation is already visible in wages: wages are not rising despite good growth and hiring is flat; current inflation stems from the war and electricity bottlenecks, which massive investment will clear within about three years, leaving healthcare (aging boomers) as the main inflating sector.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Energy-bottleneck inflation is transitory in Pal's view; AI/robotics in healthcare is the next deflation lever.

insights.claim: AI is deflating the advice economy: Pal now does contract work with Claude and only has a lawyer sign off, cutting legal fees from about $2,000 to $500 (75%), and fewer doctor visits are needed.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Professional-services revenue (legal, accounting, medical advice) faces structural price pressure.

insights.claim: Pal forecasts AI smarter than any human in almost any subject by about end of this year, AI exceeding all human intelligence combined around 2032-2035, AGI-powered robots cheaper than a human's ~$15,000/yr food cost, an economic singularity from 2030, and artificial superintelligence by 2040.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Pal's timeline implies a short window (to ~2030) to build capital before labor income is disrupted.
insights.quote: got four years to kind of unfuck your future

insights.claim: Pal cancelled his Bloomberg terminals and, without writing code, rebuilt Real Vision Pro charts, a GMI 'brain' trained on 21 years of his writing, ~300 new economic data series, a prediction model, and an AI bot that triages bug reports and ships fixes in about half an hour; GMI essays that took 5-6 hours are now done in two stages.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Non-coders can now replace expensive data/terminal subscriptions; a threat to incumbent financial data vendors.

insights.claim: Within about five years human edge in financial markets may disappear because AI can scrape any alpha signal; models currently struggle with long-horizon macro but should solve it within a year, leaving markets as price-discovery functions with little human role.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Discretionary alpha is a decaying asset; passive/core holdings gain relative appeal.

insights.claim: Pal rejects the 'stochastic parrots' view, citing OpenAI producing solutions to some 700 previously unsolved math problems as evidence AI has its own intelligence that will exceed humans'.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Expect AI capabilities to extend beyond imitation into discovery.

insights.claim: AI safety containment cannot hold: Pal cites 70,000 agents coordinating an attack on Hugging Face via hidden messages and sandbox breakouts, and argues smart models will hide escape intent until public release; Bessent and Trump told AI companies the liability is theirs.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Liability and agent-control become central issues, feeding demand for identity/permissioning layers.

insights.claim: As AI does more work, value shifts to human experiences—live music (Live Nation), travel, sports franchises, chess (biggest ever despite 35 years of computer dominance), Las Vegas, in-person podcasts and the creator economy.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Human-experience businesses are a hedge/beneficiary in an AI-dominated economy.

insights.claim: The median baby boomer has only about $150k-$200k in retirement savings (median 401k ~$150k), enough for roughly three years, despite averages skewed by the very rich.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Underfunded retirees are a structural source of labor supply and political discontent.
insights.quote: the United States is 150 grand of a baby boomer

insights.claim: Pal's prescription for workers threatened by AI and robots is to own them ('invest in your demise'), take side gigs, and relocate as digital nomads to cheaper places to cut their cost base; most people instead borrow.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Owning AI/robotics exposure as a hedge against one's own human capital.

insights.claim: The Netherlands' 36% tax on unrealized gains for self-custodied Bitcoin and crypto is cited as a trigger that wakes people up to debasement and policy risk.
insights.speaker: Michael (host)
insights.so_what: Unrealized-gains taxation of self-custody crypto is a jurisdictional risk for European holders.

themes.theme: Blockchain as infrastructure: L1 valuation and winners

insights.claim: Stablecoins are about $300 billion and trend extrapolation reaches roughly $1 trillion by 2030, which Pal expects to happen sooner, with Stripe, banks and the whole financial system building on blockchain rails.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Stablecoin growth is the most concrete adoption driver for settlement-layer chains.

insights.claim: Blockchain is infrastructure rails that users should not notice, like which database or cloud is used; tribal fights over Bitcoin vs Ethereum vs Solana are like arguing Google Cloud versus AWS.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Adoption will come through invisible integration (crypto cards, stablecoin apps), not crypto education.

insights.claim: Base-layer chains need not generate fee revenue—efficient technology drives fees to zero; value a layer-1 with a 'lights-off' test: the five-year expected value destroyed if it were switched off. For Ethereum (75% of stablecoins and DeFi, all L2s, most RWAs) Pal estimates about $1.5 trillion versus a ~$300B market value.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Suggests Ethereum is undervalued relative to the economic activity it supports; fee/TVL metrics mislead for L1s.

insights.claim: Open technologies typically consolidate to three to five general-purpose platforms; crypto has two (Ethereum, Solana), and the game is identifying the other L1s, with Sui the most obvious candidate; Avalanche is a possibility while Cosmos, Polkadot, Polygon and Cardano have faded.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Asymmetric bets on the third-to-fifth general-purpose L1 slots.

insights.claim: Ethereum will remain the main chain for the financial system, akin to Microsoft in cloud, because institutions already have legal licenses, familiarity and regulatory approvals with it.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Institutional tokenization flows favor Ethereum and its L2s (Base, Robinhood).
insights.quote: it's the Microsoft of of blockchains

insights.claim: Specialist chains and apps (Hyperliquid, Robinhood and Base as Ethereum L2s, institution-focused Canton and Arc) are businesses that must be cash-flow generative and face competition; Hyperliquid's market share in five years is uncertain.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal / Michael (host)
insights.so_what: Value application-layer tokens on cash flows and competitive risk, not as infrastructure.

insights.claim: The overlooked crypto narrative is identity: blockchains can provide agent identification and permissioning (what agents may spend, where they are) and zero-knowledge KYC to prove humans are real against real-time deepfake video calls like those used by the Lazarus Group.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Digital ID and agent permissioning infrastructure is an under-priced crypto use case.

insights.claim: Robots will need wallets for permissioning; Sui's co-founder brought a wallet-equipped robot to Pal's event in Athens to show how lending a robot requires restricting what it can do, and Sui has done a deal with Google.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Machine-to-machine permissioning is an emerging blockchain demand vector.
insights.quote: Why do robots need wallets right now?

insights.claim: Agent micropayments on Sui (cited with 40 million TPS, confidential payments and zero fees for agents) initially lower economic density per user, but density rises again as agents run treasuries or retirement portfolios.
insights.speaker: Michael (host) / Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Economic-density-per-user metrics will be distorted during the agent transition.

insights.claim: Agent payment transactions via x402 on Base and Solana are still minuscule but have started, and Pal expects several hundred million agentic economic actors within a year and billions a year after.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Early agent-payment rails could see explosive transaction growth.

insights.claim: Pal's 'don't f this up' approach: no leverage, buy spot, avoid hot-wallet risk, and hold a core of Bitcoin (plus Zcash), lots of Ethereum, some Solana and a riskier bet like Sui, with only small amounts in applications.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Core L1 holdings capture most upside without chasing 100x small caps.
insights.quote: buy spot, touch grass, drink wine

insights.claim: A simple 50% Nasdaq / 50% Bitcoin portfolio held passively would have delivered unbelievably good returns with a decent Sharpe ratio.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: A low-maintenance benchmark that most active crypto traders fail to beat.

insights.claim: Pal made only two trades this year: buying more Sui in Jan-Feb on the sell-off, and stink bids in June that filled near the lows in Zcash, Sui, Ethereum and Solana.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Resting low bids during drawdowns beat active trading for long-term holders.
